correctness.rationale: For X=(R^2,max(|u|,|v|,|u-v|)) and all real tau>=0 the hexagonal isometries R(u,v)=(u-v,u) and Q(u,v)=(u,u-v) reduce any unit pair to x=(1,s), 0<=s<=1, and four representative y edges. Two give a 1+tau facet lower bound. On the other two, the three norm-facet inequalities with nonnegative weights (1,tau^2,tau)/D and (tau,tau^2,1)/D, D=1+tau+tau^2, cancel both free edge parameters and yield F=tau+1/D. The explicit unit pair x=(1,1/D), y=(tau^2/D,1) attains F in both transformed norms, including tau=0. Symbolic sympy checks reproduced both weighted identities, the witness equalities, the cubic asymptotic and the t=1 value 4/3; independent exact Fraction grids on all four edge classes for six t values corroborate but do not replace the universal edge proof.
residual_risks: The accompanying finite rational script is not exhaustive for the continuum; universality rests on the independently reconstructed edge/facet proof.

evidence: For the published balanced maximizer x=(1,0), y=(t/(1+t),1) (0<t<=1), ||A_t(x,y)_1||=||A_t(x,y)_2||=J[t,H].

For any unit x,y with z=max ||A_t(x,y)||, the inverse-normalized pair A_t(x,y)/z lies in B_H^2, giving J>= (1+t^2)/z and then S>= (1+t^2)/J. Ball/sphere equality follows by moving one variable at a time along nonzero intersections of two supporting halfspaces, possible in dimension two.
The balanced J maximizer produces unit inputs A_t(x,y)/J with S<= (1+t^2)/J; equality plus reciprocal extension exactly recovers original formula, endpoint value and asymptotics.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The claim is a direct corollary of the exact published same-space full-parameter skew James result and an elementary transform/normalization lemma. It is not an original independent exact profile even though its direct six-edge proof is correct.

originality.rationale: A separate already published exact result for the SAME hexagonal Banach norm determines J[t,H]=sup_{x,y in S_H} min(N(x+t y),N(t x-y))=(1+t+t^2)/(1+t) for all t>0 and exhibits a balanced extremizer on 0<t<=1. For any real 2D norm, the ball supremum of the same min equals the sphere supremum (push each interior coordinate along a nonzero direction satisfying two norming-functional halfspace inequalities without decreasing either output norm). A_t^2=(1+t^2)I implies J[t,H]>= (1+t^2)/S[t,H]. The published balanced extremizer has both transformed norms J; applying A_t to its normalized output unit pair yields S[t,H]<=(1+t^2)/J. Thus S=(1+t^2)/J=(1+t)(1+t^2)/(1+t+t^2), EXACTLY the submitted formula for 0<t<=1. Reciprocal symmetry extends t>1, and S(0)=1. This is decisive theorem implication, not mere functional-name similarity or a failed search. Both publications share a dated 2026-10-11 listing; precise intra-day precedence is not claimed.
residual_risks: Resultary J profile and target S package both have reported 2026-10-11 publication dates; no intra-day first-priority order was established. The verdict is mathematical coverage by another already published finding, not a chronological claim about first authorship.

Full original Fu--Yang--Liu--Li paper was not accessible through permitted authorized route; it might contain even earlier same-object coverage. This is not used as evidence for the decisive O rejection.

The general reciprocal inequality J>= (1+t^2)/S is proved here via two-functional supporting-halfspace argument in real dimension at least two; equality requires balanced extremizers and is verified for the published exact hexagonal J. It is not asserted for all Banach spaces.
